notes: Method deviates intentionally from 20260903: instead of a Node-side bulk fetch, this run issued every request as page.fetch() executed inside chrome-devtools MCP evaluate_script on one dedicated isolated-context page (isolatedContext 'vals-ai-rescrape-20260904'), per this run's explicit browser rules. Each benchmark's raw HTML was parsed for <astro-island> elements and the one whose props JSON contains '"benchmarkView":[0,{"default":' was selected (the full-data island with metadata+tasks, including stderr/temperature/top_p/max_output_tokens/reasoning/reasoning_effort/verbosity/compute_effort/provider/harness per model per task) — the smaller ScatterGraph/BarGraph islands on the same page carry a benchmarkView without the 'default' wrapper and only 'overall', and were deliberately skipped, same distinction 20260903 documented.
Astro's [typeCode, value] prop wrapping was undone recursively (type 1 = array of wrapped items, type 0 = wrapped object/primitive) via a generic unwrap function; no value was altered.

raw.json is keyed by URL path slug (e.g. 'web_search'), matching 20260903's convention; normalized.json's benchmark_slug uses each payload's own metadata.slug, which can differ from the URL slug (web_search's metadata.slug is still 'web_search_backends').

cost_usd is cost_per_test (USD per single test case), latency_s is the site's latency (seconds); both, plus stderr and max_output_tokens, are omitted per-record when the site leaves them null, same as 20260903.

rank is computed here by sorting each benchmark's own 'overall' task accuracy values descending per model; ties/nulls are not ranked (records lacking a numeric accuracy were excluded, none were observed today).
context_window remains unpublished on vals.ai and is absent from every record.
Models are identified by the provider-qualified id the payload uses; display names are not in the payload and are not guessed.

rsi_index has no astro-island data payload (narrative report page); this run re-fetched the page and confirmed via the same island-scan that no benchmarkView payload exists for it, and confirmed the page still shows 'UPDATED 8/12/2026' with identical task-table text (model/result/score/cost) to 20260903 on visual spot-check of the fetched HTML. Its 15 records (5 task tables x 3 models, metric 'index_score') were therefore carried over verbatim from 20260903/vals-ai rather than re-scraped via live DOM, to avoid navigating the shared isolated page away from fetch-based scraping mid-run.

Two benchmarks -- Finance Agent v1.1 (slug 'finance_agent') and Terminal-Bench 1.0 (slug 'terminal-bench') -- are no longer linked from the /benchmarks index page's nav (only 40 of 43 slugs are discoverable via <a href> there now, down from all 43 presumably being linked before). Both URLs still resolve (HTTP 200) with full astro-island payloads and were fetched directly using the slugs recovered from 20260903's normalized.json; their data is included in this run's raw.json/normalized.json same as before.

ReverseEngBench (slug 'reverse_eng') was confirmed via fetch to now HTTP-redirect to /benchmarks/srebench, display name 'SRE Bench'. This is a rename, not a new benchmark: same content family, new slug and display name. benchmarks_captured above reflects the new name; no other benchmark name, slug, or count change was found. Total distinct benchmark_slug values in normalized.json: 43 (same as 20260903's benchmark count).

Method: chrome-devtools MCP, isolated page context 'vals-ai-rescrape-20260904' (renamed mid-task from an initial 'vals-ai-20260904' page per a coordinator instruction to standardize the naming across all 10 concurrent scraper agents; the first page was closed and a fresh one opened under the new name). Heavy page-selection contention was observed from the other 9 concurrently running agents: several select_page/evaluate_script and one navigate_page call landed on the wrong page mid-run (once on this agent's own side, hitting another agent's 'terminal-bench-20260904' page and unintentionally navigating it to /benchmarks/finance_agent; and the reverse happened to this agent's own page at least twice, observed via location.href mismatches on verification). All benchmark-data fetches were absolute-URL page.fetch() calls, which returned correct vals.ai content even on the occasions the executing page had been navigated elsewhere by another agent, since vals.ai appears to serve permissive CORS; nonetheless every fetch batch was re-verified for internal consistency (record counts, model-id shapes) before being written.
changes_vs_20260903: Total row_count rose from 2750 to 2762 (+12), driven by newly-added per-model rows on existing benchmarks (see below), not new benchmarks: distinct benchmark_slug count is unchanged at 43.
ReverseEngBench (reverse_eng) renamed to SRE Bench (srebench); old URL 302s to the new one. No other benchmark added, removed, or renamed.
Finance Agent v1.1 (finance_agent) and Terminal-Bench 1.0 (terminal-bench) dropped off the /benchmarks index page's own nav links but their pages and data are still live and were still captured.

meta/muse_spark_1_3 (or any 'Muse Spark 1.3' display name/id) is still absent from every benchmark today, same as 20260902 and 20260903; the newest Muse Spark id on the site remains meta/muse_spark_1_2 (present, e.g. Code Migration 29.954/rank 24, CorpFin v2 70.94/rank 5, Finance Agent (v2) 60.599/rank 2, SWE-bench 86.6/rank 14).

google/gemini-3.8-flash is present today (25 records across benchmarks; e.g. Code Migration 36.546/rank 19/stderr 4.184, Finance Agent (v2) 61.435/rank 1/stderr 0.128, SWE-bench 80/rank 24/stderr 1.791) but has no CorpFin v2 row (confirmed absent from all 134 CorpFin v2 models, not merely missing accuracy).
